# Commit ID map (history rewrite, 2026-10-07)

Before the repository was made public, every commit's author and committer
email was changed to GitHub's private no-reply address. Commit contents did
not change - every commit has exactly the same files as before - but every
commit ID did, because a commit's ID covers its author.

IDs written in commit messages were translated automatically. IDs written in
files were translated in one commit on `release/rc.11`; files kept verbatim
on purpose (the macOS results transcripts) and names that embed an ID
(`OTTER_MACOS_RESULTS_bb43658.md`, certification record folders such as
`20261006T235517Z-1b1c492`, branches such as `mac-results/bb43658`) still show
the old ID. Look any old ID up here; a prefix is enough.

The tag `v1.0.0-rc.9` was not carried over: it pointed at `856b9b5` (old ID),
not at the rc.9 candidate `b8d9190` (old ID), which was never tagged.
